rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track. Progress was only 0.035 to 0.115, with one line-loss event per run. Max error sat at about 0.061 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and rms error was about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation was low (about 0.07), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily off the line early in each course rather than oscillating. The most likely cause is the fixed 2% left/right motor mismatch. With ki = 0, proportional control alone leaves a steady heading offset that grows until the robot leaves the tape. Base speed 1.6 may also be too fast to correct that drift on the first bends. Changes: (1) controller.ki from 0 to 0.3, to remove the steady offset caused by the motor mismatch; the integral is clamped at +/-2, so the contribution stays bounded. (2) controller.base_speed from 1.6 to 1.3, to give the loop more time to correct and reduce line loss. (3) controller.kp from 2.5 to 3.0, for a stiffer response to the measured offset. (4) controller.kd from 0.05 to 0.15, to damp the stiffer response and avoid overshoot. Geometry is unchanged, so the race isolates the controller. Expected result: fewer or no line-loss events, progress well above 0.2 on the oval and s-bend, and max_error under about 0.04 m. Completion within 3 s is not expected yet, because base_speed 1.3 is below the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed. Hypotheses to test next: (a) the motor mismatch causes a steady offset that ki removes; (b) the early off-track exit comes from overshoot on the first bends, which kd addresses. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and completion_time. If progress reaches about 0.995 with no line loss, raise base_speed toward 1.8 next. If the run still drifts with a steady bias, raise ki before touching kp.
